questions.question: Which characteristic of living organisms specifically refers to the permanent removal of metabolic waste products, such as carbon dioxide, that are produced during cellular chemical reactions?

options.text: Secretion
Egestion
Digestion
Excretion

questions.explanation: Excretion is defined as the removal of toxic metabolic waste substances formed during cellular metabolism (such as carbon dioxide and urea). In contrast, egestion is the expulsion of undigested dietary food residues from the digestive tract.

questions.question: In the standard Linnaean taxonomic hierarchy of biological classification, which rank is placed directly between Phylum and Order?

options.text: Family
Genus
Class
Species

questions.explanation: The biological classification hierarchy in descending order is Domain, Kingdom, Phylum (or Division for plants), Class, Order, Family, Genus, and Species. Thus, Class directly connects Phylum and Order.

questions.question: According to the international rules of binomial nomenclature introduced by Carolus Linnaeus, how must a scientific name be formatted when printed?

options.text: Both the genus and specific epithet begin with capital letters and appear in bold font
The genus begins with a lowercase letter and the specific epithet is fully capitalized in plain font
The specific epithet is placed first in italics followed by the capitalized genus name in quotation marks
The genus name begins with a capital letter, the specific epithet starts with a lowercase letter, and both parts are italicized

questions.explanation: Under binomial nomenclature, the scientific name consists of two parts: the genus name, which is always capitalized, and the specific epithet, which always begins with a lowercase letter. When printed, both words must be italicized (or underlined when handwritten).

questions.question: Unlike plant cell walls which are built primarily of cellulose, the rigid cell walls of organisms belonging to Kingdom Fungi are composed of:

options.text: Peptidoglycan
Chitin and polysaccharides
Collagen and silica
Glycogen and phospholipids

questions.explanation: A distinguishing characteristic of Kingdom Fungi is that their cell walls are reinforced with chitin and structural polysaccharides, unlike plants (cellulose) and bacteria (peptidoglycan).

questions.question: Which renowned Ethiopian botanist contributed significantly to the publication of the 'Flora of Ethiopia' and served as the director of the Gullele Botanical Garden?

options.text: Professor Sebsebe Demissew
Dr. Melaku Worede
Professor Tilahun Yilma
Dr. Aklilu Lemma

questions.explanation: Professor Sebsebe Demissew is a distinguished Ethiopian taxonomist who led research projects on African vegetation, served as director of the Flora of Ethiopia and the Gullele Botanical Garden, and held leadership roles in international taxonomic associations.

questions.question: Which of the following cellular features correctly distinguishes organisms in the domain Archaea from those in the domain Bacteria?

options.text: Archaea contain linear chromosomes packaged with histones, whereas Bacteria possess membrane-bound nuclei
Archaea lack peptidoglycan in their cell walls, whereas true Bacteria have cell walls containing peptidoglycan
Archaea are multicellular eukaryotic organisms, whereas Bacteria are strictly unicellular prokaryotes
Archaea reproduce solely through meiosis, whereas Bacteria divide exclusively by mitosis

questions.explanation: While both Archaea and Bacteria are prokaryotes with circular chromosomes and no membrane-bound nucleus, they differ fundamentally in cell wall biochemistry: bacterial cell walls contain peptidoglycan, whereas archaeal cell walls completely lack peptidoglycan.

questions.question: Under the biological species concept, a group of organisms is defined as belonging to the same species if its members:

options.text: Can naturally interbreed with one another to produce viable, fertile offspring
Inhabit the exact same geographic region and consume identical dietary resources
Exhibit identical body size, outward coloration, and anatomical proportions
Possess the same physiological tolerance limits to abiotic environmental stress

questions.explanation: In biological taxonomy, a biological species is fundamentally defined as a population or group of populations whose members have the potential to interbreed in nature and produce viable, fertile offspring.

questions.question: Ethiopia is globally recognized as a primary centre of origin and genetic diversity for which pair of agricultural crops?

options.text: Rubber tree (Hevea brasiliensis) and cassava (Manihot esculenta)
Maize (Zea mays) and soybean (Glycine max)
Tef (Eragrostis tef) and noug (Guizotia abyssinica)
Rice (Oryza sativa) and potato (Solanum tuberosum)

questions.explanation: Due to its diverse topography and climate, Ethiopia is a recognized primary centre of diversity for field crops including indigenous domesticates such as tef (Eragrostis tef), noug (Guizotia abyssinica), and Ethiopian mustard (Brassica carinata).

questions.question: Diatoms are photosynthetic unicellular protists whose silica-rich microscopic shells accumulate as diatomite rock. Which industrial application directly utilizes diatomite?

options.text: Synthesizing inorganic ammonium nitrate fertilizers for soil enrichment
Serving as a microbial bioinsecticide against agricultural crop borers
Acting as a fermenting agent to raise traditional bread dough
Serving as an absorbent agent for chemical spills and an abrasive in polishing cleaners

questions.explanation: Diatomite is a powdery, porous sedimentary deposit formed from fossilized diatom cell walls. Because it is highly absorbent and mildly abrasive, it is widely used in chemical spill cleanup, pet litter, filtration, and household polishing agents.

questions.question: A student examines a plant that possesses true roots, stems, and leaves with well-developed vascular tissues (xylem and phloem), but reproduces solely via spores without ever producing cones, flowers, or seeds. To which division does this plant belong?

options.text: Bryophyta
Pteridophyta
Gymnospermae
Angiospermae

questions.explanation: Pteridophytes (such as ferns) are seedless vascular plants that have true vegetative organs and vascular conduction tissues, but reproduce using spores rather than seeds.

questions.question: Which combination of nutritional and structural characteristics uniquely distinguishes organisms in Kingdom Animalia from both plants and fungi?

options.text: Autotrophic nutrition, cellulose cell walls, and chloroplast-containing cells
Absorptive heterotrophy, chitinous cell walls, and filamentous hyphae
Ingestive heterotrophy, lack of cell walls, and structural support provided by collagen
Chemosynthetic nutrition, presence of peptidoglycan walls, and lack of membrane organelles

questions.explanation: Animals are multicellular heterotrophs that ingest food before digesting it internally. Unlike plants and fungi, animal cells completely lack cell walls and are held together by structural proteins, predominantly collagen.

questions.question:
A student identifies an unknown vertebrate using the following dichotomous key steps:
1. Poikilothermic (go to 2) / Homoiothermic (go to 4)
2. Has fins but no limbs (Fish) / Has four limbs (go to 3)
3. Has no scales on body (Amphibian) / Has scales or shell (Reptile)
4. Has feathers (Bird) / Has fur (Mammal)
If the specimen has a fluctuating body temperature dependent on the surroundings, four walking limbs, and smooth, moist skin completely lacking scales, which class does it belong to?

options.text: Reptile
Amphibian
Mammal
Fish

questions.explanation: Following the key: being cold-blooded (poikilothermic) directs to step 2; having four limbs rather than fins directs to step 3; having four limbs with skin lacking scales leads directly to the identification of an Amphibian.

questions.question: Why did modern biologists find the historical two-kingdom classification scheme (Plantae and Animalia) inadequate, leading Whittaker to propose the five-kingdom system in 1969?

options.text: It failed to distinguish prokaryotes from eukaryotes, unicellular from multicellular forms, and photosynthetic plants from absorptive fungi
It incorrectly classified flying birds, bats, and insects together into a single taxonomic order
It classified non-living pathogenic viruses as photosynthetic autotrophs within Kingdom Plantae
It completely omitted macroscopic plants and focused exclusively on single-celled bacteria

questions.explanation: The early two-kingdom system was deemed inadequate because it placed fundamentally different organisms into the same group. It did not differentiate between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cellular organization, unicellular and multicellular bodies, or autotrophic green plants and heterotrophic saprophytic fungi.

questions.question: A biology student compares maize (Zea mays) with a faba bean plant. Which pair of morphological characteristics correctly distinguishes maize (a monocotyledon) from the faba bean (a dicotyledon)?

options.text: Maize has an embryo with two cotyledons and reticulate leaf venation; faba bean has a single cotyledon and parallel leaf venation
Maize develops naked seeds born on exposed scales; faba bean develops seeds inside closed fleshy berries
Maize has an embryo with a single cotyledon and leaves with parallel veins; faba bean has two cotyledons and branching (net-like) veins
Maize lacks conducting vascular bundles; faba bean contains xylem and phloem in its stems and roots

questions.explanation: Monocotyledons (such as maize) are characterized by having a single seed leaf (cotyledon) in the embryo and leaves with parallel venation. Dicotyledons (such as faba bean) have two cotyledons and reticulate (branching/net-like) leaf venation.

questions.question: Although both fungi and animals are heterotrophic eukaryotes, they obtain nourishment through fundamentally different mechanisms. How do saprophytic fungi acquire organic nutrients from their environment?

options.text: They ingest solid food particles into internal digestive cavities via phagocytosis
They utilize bacteriochlorophyll pigments to synthesize organic compounds from dead substrates in the dark
They absorb intact, unhydrolyzed starch and protein polymers directly through specialized root hairs
They secrete extracellular hydrolytic enzymes through their hyphae to digest substrates externally, then absorb the soluble nutrients

questions.explanation: Unlike animals that ingest food and digest it internally, fungi perform extracellular digestion. Their hyphae release hydrolytic enzymes into the surrounding substrate to break down complex polymers into simple soluble molecules, which are then absorbed across their cell membranes.
